```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 18
    n_vehicles = 5
    Q = 76  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[57, 27], [54, 34], [28, 8], [73, 67], [34, 34], [65, 56], [22, 5], [37, 18], [86, 56], [48, 60], [56, 67], [75, 36], [35, 7], [94, 56], [57, 41], [94, 56], [89, 65], [90, 19]]
    demands = [21, 11, 11, 15, 6, 11, 17, 19, 19, 15, 6, 15, 8, 24, 7, 18, 23, 8]
    time_windows = [[0, 325], [21, 100], [15, 81], [67, 135], [28, 100], [41, 141], [38, 96], [55, 108], [46, 142], [50, 147], [5, 71], [23, 101], [52, 108], [60, 124], [42, 102], [10, 107], [65, 115], [58, 157], [59, 126]]
    service_times = [13, 10, 6, 15, 7, 12, 6, 14, 5, 6, 5, 5, 10, 12, 15, 12, 9, 7]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Daily vehicle routing and scheduling with customer time windows

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a central depot to serve a set of customers distributed across the service area. All vehicles will depart the depot at time 0, visit assigned customers, and return to the depot before it closes for the day. The travel time between any two locations is taken as the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1, so distance units equal time units.

The Routing and Scheduling Challenge
We need to design a set of delivery routes and service start times that collectively visit every customer exactly once while meeting both capacity and time constraints. Each vehicle will make a single trip: it leaves the depot at time 0, visits a sequence of customers, and returns to the depot before the closing time. The routing must balance the trade-off between consolidating stops on fewer vehicles and ensuring on-time service within the customers’ delivery windows.

Requirements and Operating Rules
- Fleet and trips:
  - Vehicles are identical and can be deployed selectively; not all vehicles must be used.
  - Each deployed vehicle performs a single outbound tour and must be back at the depot before it closes.
- Customer service with time windows:
  - Every customer has an earliest and latest acceptable delivery start time. Service must begin within that window.
  - If a vehicle arrives before a customer’s window opens, it must wait on site until the window opens; if it arrives after the latest acceptable time, that stop is considered late and is not allowed.
  - Each customer requires a specified unloading/service duration; the vehicle departs a stop immediately after completing that service.
- Capacity constraints:
  - Each vehicle has a maximum carrying capacity. The total demand assigned to any vehicle’s route must not exceed its capacity at any point. There is no mid-route replenishment.
- Travel time and distances:
  - Travel time between any two locations equals the straight-line distance between their coordinates. Because speed is set to 1, routing time and distance are interchangeable for planning.
- Costs:
  - The total cost of an operating plan is the sum of distance-based travel costs and a fixed deployment cost for each vehicle used. This creates a trade-off between using additional vehicles to satisfy tighter windows and keeping distance-driven costs down.

Planning Objective
Build a set of routes and schedules that:
- Visit every customer exactly once.
- Respect all customer time windows, including waiting if early.
- Observe service times at each stop.
- Keep the load on each route within vehicle capacity.
- Ensure all vehicles depart at time 0 and return to the depot before it closes.
- Minimize the total travel distance plus fixed vehicle deployment costs.

Implementation Notes
- Sequencing decisions should account for potential waiting at early arrivals to avoid late service starts at subsequent stops.
- Route design should avoid overloading any vehicle and ensure that the final leg returns to the depot before closure.
- Because deploying a vehicle incurs a fixed cost, solutions should balance route consolidation with on-time delivery performance.
